beats.t: Before they reached the island, the lotus-leaf boat caught in a clump of reeds. Yeongnyangi pressed a paw against the current. Amid the clinking mirror shards came a faint grinding of teeth. Yeoni pricked up their pig ears. It almost sounded like someone holding back tears.
There's a black fluffball under those reeds. Wait. It has eyes.

A little cloak edged with gold thread was tangled in the reeds. A striped tail wriggled beneath it. A black tiger. Even wet, its red eyes were bright, and the marking on its forehead glowed red as a wound. A black loop finer than thread encircled its right forepaw.
If you've finished staring, please leave. And I am not a fluffball. Would you kindly take that back?
You can talk too. Then ask for help. Your paw's shaking.
Don't touch it. It isn't a trap.
It's a ring seeking an owner. It asks your name, and binds you if you answer.

Yeoni stopped her outstretched hoof. Neither the body nor the name she could return to was certain yet. But she could see the ring tighten with every breath the tiger took. Leaving that one paw behind felt more frightening than stopping.
Then I just won't say my name. Yeongnyangi, hold the boat steady.
The complicated stuff can wait. I'm scared too.

Yeoni picked up a dry leaf stalk from the boat's edge in their mouth. Black water spurted as they pushed it between the ring and the fur. The tiger reflexively lashed at Yeoni's nose, then stopped. The stalk snapped. The ring was still tight.
Please stop. You can barely manage your own body. Whom do you think you're saving?
If you get hurt, do you intend to charge me for it?
If it hurts, say it hurts. Stop putting a price tag on everything.
I didn't negotiate this long when I dropped my rice triangle.

Gold gathered at the tips of Yeongnyangi's claws. A direct cut at that angle would injure the tiger's paw too. Yeongnyangi withdrew the blade-like light and tilted the leaf. The current changed direction. For one brief instant, the taut ring loosened.
Now. Don't pull. Push.
Don't remove the ring. Make room for the paw to slip out.

Yeoni pressed their forehead against the tiger's shoulder. They rolled together onto the wet leaf. The ring stayed behind in the river and contracted, clutching at empty air. It bit three times at the place the paw had been, then burst into black foam.
Why push with your own body, dear guest? You could have ordered that cat in the hat.
That's how you're meant to use the power to command.
Why call asking a friend an order?
A pig's forehead is useful. The nose just hurts uselessly.
The tiger studied the scrape on Yeoni's nose. Red eyes narrowed as she tugged her cloak. Each time Yeoni winced, the tip of the tiger's tail twitched, as though counting.
The red eyes moved from the scrape to her crown. Of the flower's five petals, one alone was washed white. The tiger's gaze lingered there.
That petal has already paid its price, I see. You seem to have settled an account elsewhere first.
Please tell me what you want. A path, or an object. Either will do.
Debts grow when left unpaid.
As long as you're okay. If I had to ask for something, your name. You look like you'd get mad if I called you Tiger.
A name is not something to give away lightly. Whoever holds it can call you from anywhere.
A life spent coming whenever you're called is hardly pleasant.
Then I'll just call you Tiger. I can help without knowing your name.

The tiger's tail went still. A droplet fell from the gold clasp and rolled across the leaf. Yeongnyangi saw it crawl toward the tiger instead of returning to the river. Without a word, a paw came down between Yeoni and the tiger.
Only as far as the landing. I won't ask who sent you.
Don't ask this girl's name either.
Are all cats in hats this curt? One little paw freed, and already you're putting up fences.
Afraid I might bite our guest?
I thought he was a big cat at first too, but he hates that. Do you hate being called a little tiger?
Kindly leave out the little. Count the cloak, and I'm not so small.
Ranking people by size is rather an outdated taste.

Yeoni laughed. Rather than join in, the tiger lowered her ears, hiding their flushed insides under her cloak. Yeoni softened her voice. The tiger's tail twitched again, as though taking notes and counting even each laugh.
Sit over there, where it's dry. Your cloak must be heavy with water.
All that gold trim looks great, but washing it must be a nightmare.

The tiger held out the cloak's hem. A black thread hidden inside the gold edging slipped among the fabric's red fibers. When Yeongnyangi turned, it stopped. The tiger licked its wet paw as though nothing had happened.
Press it to your nose. I haven't given you the cloak, so please don't mistake it for yours.
Right. Borrowing it. You talk scary, but your paws are kind.

The island bell rang. The tiger pricked up her ears at the first note and jumped off before the second. Her injured paw never touched water. The black surface briefly hardened into a narrow path beneath each step. She crossed without looking back.
Don't follow those tracks. Anyone who can make a road on water didn't get trapped for lack of a path.
You mean she got caught on purpose? I thought the pain on her face was real.
Pain can be real and still hide another motive. Look at both.
That doesn't make helping her wrong.

Yeoni pulled a red strand from the cloak off their nose and laid it on a hoof. Somehow, they could not throw it away. Beyond the island mist, the black tiger looked back. Its smile was gone. Only two red points remained above the water.
So you stop whenever you see someone hurt. Now I know whom to put in your path.
Next time, please come without that cat.

The ring's pain had been real. A broken black thread sank from the cloak into the river. Beneath it, someone's name silently vanished. Yeoni didn't see. Only the scrap resting on her hoof remained strangely warm.
